title: Koki Beans (Steamed Black-Eyed Pea Pudding)
author: Imma Adamu (Immaculate Bites)
desc: Skinless black-eyed peas pureed with palm oil, onion, pepper, water and bouillon, folded with spinach, wrapped in banana leaves and foil and steamed about 1 hour 30 minutes.
longDesc: Adamu, who writes that she grew up in Cameroon, calls it koki beans, ekoki, haricots koki and bean cakes. The skinless black-eyed peas are soaked about 2 hours (or up to 24) until fully hydrated. Palm oil is warmed a minute or two until completely melted. The peas, onion, pepper, water and bouillon are pulsed to a puree that is ‘just a little gritty’, the spinach folded in, about 2 cups placed on each leaf, wrapped in foil, and steamed about an hour and a half, then cooled about 10 minutes before serving.
ingredients: 2 Maggi cubes or 2 teaspoons (7 g) bouillon powder
3 teaspoons (15–20 g) salt, or more to taste
Banana leaves and foil — quantity not printed
steps: Soak the black-eyed peas about 2 hours, or up to 24 hours, until fully hydrated.
Warm the palm oil about a minute or two until completely melted.
Pulse the peas with the onion, pepper, water, bouillon and salt to a puree that is just a little gritty, using up all the water.
Put about 2 cups of the mixture on each banana leaf, wrap in foil and steam about 1 hour 30 minutes, adding water as needed.
chefTips: The printed texture cue is ‘just a little gritty’ puree.
Add water to the steamer as needed during the long steam.
No doneness cue is printed beyond the time.
healthBenefits: Black-eyed peas provide plant protein and fibre; the palm oil is a large fat contributor.
culturalNote: The author writes that she grew up in Cameroon; the page does not name a community. Banana leaves and foil are used in the method but not quantified in the ingredient list.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Koki Beans’. Byline as printed: ‘Imma Adamu’. Published 9 Sep 2025, last update 26 Sep 2025. Yield 6. Prep 30 min, cook 1 h 30 min, soak 2 h, total 4 h. TWO-PASS.
Disagreements recorded, not reconciled: steam time (about 1 h 30 here; 4 h in CMR022; 2 h in CMR023) and oil ratio (1 cup to 280–300 g peas here; 30 cl to 500 g beans in CMR022).
